children: Today's sharp selloff in stocks is fueling a flight-to-quality rally in U.S. Treasurys, with yields dropping to their lowest levels since early September.
The yield on the 10-year Treasury note hit as low as 4.822% in recent trading, according to Tradeweb. That was the lowest since Sept. 9 when yields were on an upward trajectory.
Some analysts said that today's rally in bonds reflected more a knee-jerk reaction to stock selloff than a fundamental reassessment of the outlook for economic growth and interest rates.

Interest-rate futures show that traders still expect the Federal Reserve to raise short-term rates at its final meeting of the year next month. However, the chances of a hike have dropped to 69% from 83% yesterday, according to CME Group data.
